skill.description: Schedule Google Calendar meetings through Rarefriend, resolve attendees from contacts, find available time, manage events, and record meeting notes.
skill.summary: Manage Google Calendar scheduling and meeting context through Rarefriend.
skill.author: Whitefield-Labs

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mainly Markdown backtick, setup-path, and hardcoded-link false positives in documentation. I found no prompt injection or hidden execution intent. The remaining concern is that setup examples place OAuth client secrets in command and config contexts.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer setup guidance that reads secrets from environment variables or a secret store, not inline command arguments.
Explain where MCP clients store Rarefriend client secrets and advise users to protect those config files.

semantic_findings.description: Setup instructions show RAREFRIEND_CLIENT_SECRET in a Claude MCP command and MCP config examples. Users may copy real secrets into shell history or local config files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines explicitly show RAREFRIEND_CLIENT_SECRET in command and configuration examples. The examples use placeholders, so the risk depends on users substituting real values.

content.value_statement: Manual scheduling across contacts and calendars can create conflicts and missing context. This skill helps agents check availability, resolve attendees, create events, and record meeting notes through Rarefriend and Google Calendar.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether Rarefriend MCP and Google Calendar are connected.
Lists upcoming Google Calendar events with optional limits and date windows.
Searches calendar events by keyword and time range.
Finds available slots and checks attendee availability when emails are known.
Creates, reschedules, or cancels Google Calendar events after user confirmation.
Resolves contact names and records meeting notes through Rarefriend contact tools.
limitations: Requires Rarefriend MCP with a valid client ID and client secret.
Requires the user to connect Google Calendar before event tools work.
Can only schedule attendees whose emails are found or provided.
Depends on Rarefriend permissions, Google permissions, and sync state.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Executive Meetings
use_cases.description: Find open slots, resolve contact emails, and create events without switching between calendar and contact tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Follow Ups
use_cases.description: Search prior contact notes, schedule customer calls, and log new meeting context after each conversation.

use_cases.title: Manage Team Availability
use_cases.description: Check team schedules, find shared free time, and move meetings when priorities change.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Week
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my Google Calendar for this week. Group events by day and highlight meetings with multiple attendees.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule A Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Schedule a 30 minute call with Alice next week. Resolve her email, find free times, and ask me before booking.

prompt_templates.title: Find Group Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a 45 minute slot for Maya, Jordan, and me on Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon. Show the best options first.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare And Log Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my next meeting with Marcus, show relevant recent notes, and help me add follow-up notes after the call.

output_examples.input: Find time with Alice next week for 30 minutes.
output_examples.output: I found Alice in Google Contacts. You are both free Tuesday at 10:00 AM and Wednesday at 2:00 PM. Which slot should I book?

output_examples.input: What is on my calendar today?
output: The busiest period is 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM.
Your 10:30 AM meeting has three attendees.

output_examples.input: Move my project review to Friday afternoon.
output_examples.output: I found the project review event. Friday at 2:30 PM is open. Please confirm before I reschedule it.

best_practices: Confirm attendee email, time zone, and final slot before creating an event.
Check availability before every new meeting to avoid calendar conflicts.
Use clear event titles and add useful context in descriptions or notes.
anti_patterns: Do not create meetings before resolving ambiguous contact names.
Do not store real client secrets in shared chat transcripts.
Do not use transparent events for meetings that should block availability.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Rarefriend MCP and Google Calendar. Rarefriend also provides contact lookup and meeting notes.

faq.question: Can it schedule meetings with contacts by name?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search Rarefriend contacts, find an email, and use that email for calendar availability.

faq.question: Does it create events automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow asks for confirmation before booking suggested time slots.

faq.question: Can it check attendee availability?
faq.answer: Yes. It can pass attendee emails to Rarefriend calendar tools when those emails are known.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need Rarefriend MCP credentials and a connected Google Calendar integration.

faq.question: Can it manage notes after meetings?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create and search Rarefriend notes for contacts linked to meetings.
